newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine Druzhba pipeline carries less, earns more.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine Druzhba pipeline carries less, earns more.

text.p: Ukraine's section of the Druzhba (Friendship) oil pipeline carrying Russian supplies to Eastern and Central Europe earned more money in 1996 despite carrying less oil, a top official said on Monday.

Lyubomyr Bunyak, director of the Ukrainian portion of the link, also said in an interview that Druzhba transported 16.63 million tonnes of Russian oil last year and earned $86.5 million from transit fees, compared to 18.0 million tonnes in 1995 and $81.40 in earnings.

Bunyak said that last year, 6.21 million tonnes of oil were sent to the Czech Republic, 5.22 million tonnes to Slovakia and 5.21 million tonnes to Hungary. A small amount of oil went to the former Yugoslavia, mostly to Serbia and Slovenia.
Druzhba's total capacity, including the Belarussian stretch to Poland and Germany, is about 60 million tonnes.
But the link has been under-utilised since the 1991 break-up of the former Soviet superpower, when many European clients diversified their energy supplies.
Bunyak said the pipeline would not alter its transit tariff in 1997.
Last year, Ukraine caused a row with Russia when it raised the tariff to $5.20 per tonne of oil transported across the whole Ukrainian stretch of the link from $4.75 per tonne.

"There is no point in doing that," Bunyak said. "Now we have a stable currency in Ukraine with low inflation. "Also there is no need for change because of political reasons. We should not damage relations with Russia."
Russia's Fuel and Energy Ministry still disagrees with Ukraine's tariff.
Bunyak said Druzhba had signed 25 contracts for supplies in 1997 supplies and that dozens more were in the works.
"We will work stably. We expect to pump 1.35 million tonnes of oil in January," he said.
He said the pipeline spent $6 million for computerisation and modernisation of a stretch through the Carpathian mountains in western Ukraine.
